_comment: Shared cross-language corpus for the bandcamp_embed_url gates (PSY-1966).
THE CONTRACT: anything the Go write gate stores must be renderable by the
frontend read gate. Nothing may be storable and unrenderable, or a curator's
Go reads this file in utils.TestBandcampURLCorpus; TypeScript reads the same
file in frontend/lib/bandcamp.test.ts. Both assert their own half, so a
change to either predicate that breaks the contract fails on that side and
names the value. Editing one language's rules without editing this file is
what the two tests are here to catch — a hand-copied list in one test file
could not, and missed the backslash divergence until a review found it.
marks the ones the reader must ALSO refuse, i.e. the parser
divergences that made this contract non-obvious. The rest are
cases where the writer is deliberately the stricter side.

rejected.why: percent-encoded first segment; Go's decoded Path would say /album/y
encoded slash; decoded it looks like a release path
dot segments the browser resolves to /evil
backslash is a segment delimiter to WHATWG, an ordinary byte to Go; browser resolves to /gift-card
encoded dot-dot behind a backslash
foreign host wearing a release-shaped path
lookalike suffix
lookalike prefix
userinfo spoofing the host
open redirect carrying a real release URL
profile root, not a release
on-platform, but the release segment is only in the query
http renders nothing: neither the resolver nor the link gate accepts it
non-http scheme
whitespace-only would be stored blank-but-not-null
the apex is not an artist page. The READER accepts it, deliberately, so a legacy row still renders; this is the one delta where the read gate is the lenient side
leading space; the browser strips it, so the reader accepts. Refused on write so the stored string is exactly what was validated
trailing space; survives url.Parse and would otherwise be stored, then never equal the trimmed URL the release-derived recompute produces
encoded 'a' plus a non-ASCII slug: EscapedPath re-escapes to /album/caf%C3%A9 and would pass; browser pathname keeps /%61lbum/
encoded 'a' plus a space: same EscapedPath fallback
encoded slash plus a non-ASCII slug: the fallback turns %2F back into a real /
encoded slash plus a space: same fallback
fully encoded 'album' plus a space
